page.title: Statements
page.purpose: Answer income-versus-expense over a period and assets-minus-liabilities at a date, as queries over the journal — and produce the categorised export an accountant can use.

priorities.statement: The statement figures for the selected period or date
Whether the period is fully covered by available sources, and where it is not
That these are categorisations, never tax computations
Export and period selection, ranked below the three above

states.description: A statement rendered for the selected period.
Nothing in flight; the surface is at rest and its controls are usable.
A user-triggered operation is in flight and its outcome is not yet known.
An operation completed; the result is announced, not merely rendered.
First read of the surface's data; layout is reserved so nothing shifts on arrival.
A write is in flight; the affected control is disabled and says why.
A background read is refreshing data the user is already looking at.
A user-requested re-read of data already on screen.
The period contains no events at all. Distinct from a period whose sources could not be read.
Some contributing source could not be read; what is missing is named.
Displayed data is older than its freshness window; its age is shown.
Input was rejected before submission; the offending field is identified.
The request failed; the reason and the next action are stated.
An automatic retry is in progress; attempt count and next attempt are visible.
The caller's role does not permit this; what role would is stated.
The client cannot reach the API; queued or read-only behavior is explained.
An adapter was unavailable for part of the selected period, so the statement covers less than the period claims. The uncovered span is named.
Events in the period carry no deductibility category. Surfaced before export, because an export of silently uncategorised events is worse than no export.

elements.name: Statement
elements.description: Income versus expense for a period, or assets minus liabilities at a date. Figures are compared down the column.
Whether every day in the selected period was covered by available sources, and which span was not.

elements.name: Period
elements.description: The period or as-at date the statement is computed for.

elements.name: Categories
elements.description: Deductibility category tags rolled up. Categorisation only — no computed tax amount appears anywhere.
How many events in the period carry no category, shown before any export control.
States that these are categorisations for an accountant, not a tax computation or filing.

elements.name: Export
elements.description: Produces the accountant-facing export of the current statement and its categories.
Explains that the period contains no events, distinct from sources being unreadable.

claims.statement: When a source was unavailable for part of the period, the statement names the uncovered span rather than presenting a whole-period total.
claims.rationale: A statement is the figure most likely to be taken to a third party. A total that silently covers 26 of 31 days is the most consequential silent-zero in the product.

claims.statement: A statement covering an incomplete period is perceivably different from one covering a complete period.
claims.rationale: The honesty rule applied to the surface where a wrong number does the most external damage.

claims.statement: A period with genuinely no events is perceivably different from a period whose sources could not be read.
claims.rationale: 'You earned nothing' and 'I could not tell what you earned' are opposite conclusions that both render as an absence of rows.

claims.statement: The count of uncategorised events reads before the export control.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-006 promises an accountant a clean export. Exporting silently uncategorised events breaks that promise in a way the recipient discovers, not the operator.

claims.statement: The category breakdown is accompanied by a statement that these are categorisations rather than a tax computation.
claims.rationale: PRD non-goal: no tax computation or filing, ever — categorise, never compute. A category total sitting alone will be read as a tax figure, which is precisely the liability the non-goal avoids.

claims.statement: Statement figures share a decimal alignment and use tabular numerals.
claims.rationale: DESIGN.md binding adaptation; this page is almost entirely a column of compared figures.

claims.statement: Any chart on this page is accompanied by an equivalent table of the same figures.
claims.rationale: PRD accessibility rule: every chart has a table equivalent.
